originalTitle: Australia news live: landmark Icac inquiry into corruption allegations in NSW Liberals begins
content: Brothers of former NSW premier sought to leverage their influence to help Sydney developer, ICAC hears Returning to the NSW Icac’s Operation Rosny, counsel assisting, Dr Peggy Dwyer SC, has described the allegations being investigated in greater detail. In describing the timeline of the watchdog’s investigations, she has revealed that police referred WhatsApp communications from Jean-Claude and Charles Perrottet, two of the brothers of the former premier, Dominic Perrottet, two days before the premier himself referred allegations of corruption to Icac. The former premier made that move after a 2022 speech in parliament by the Liberal MP for Kellyville, Ray Williams, claiming that fugitive property developer Jean Nassif had met with senior Liberals, who were allegedly paid significant funds to arrange for new councillors to be elected to the Hills Shire council. Dwyer has told the hearing that the day before Williams’ speech, police referred legally intercepted communications from “not one but two of Dominic Perrottet’s brothers” to Icac. That lawfully intercepted information also indicated that Mr Nasif had an association with not one but two of Dominic Perrottet’s brothers, and that he was seeking to leverage their connections with Dominic Perrottet to assist in having the building commissioner David Chandler removed from office. Dominic Perrottet is not accused of any wrongdoing. Jean-Claude and Charles Perrottet and Nassif have previously denied any wrongdoing. The Independent Commission Against Corruption (Icac) has begun its Operation Rosny hearings into allegations of corruption in the NSW Liberals today. As part of Operation Rosny, Icac is investigating three allegations, firstly that senior Liberal figures “solicited or accepted” donations, including from prohibited donors, in amounts which were undeclared or exceeded caps, to recruit or renew members to the party – a practice known as “branch stacking”. In her opening statement, the counsel assisting the commission, Dr Peggy Dwyer SC, has said: Money in politics, as in other spheres of life, has the potential to corrupt. At a local, state, and federal level, electoral funding laws play a vital role in minimizing. minimizing the risk of corruption by ensuring transparency and attempting to level the playing field. They also promote public confidence in a fair go for politicians and political aspirants, and for the public they are entrusted to serve. A group of Victorian ministers and MPs from across Labor’s left and right factions have gone to see the premier, Jacinta Allan, to inform her that she has lost the majority of support in the caucus and urge her to stand down. Federal opposition leader Angus Taylor has said the prime minister should be “sitting down with” US president Donald Trump after the US hit Australian exports with new 12.5% trade tariffs, claiming the country is not doing enough to combat forced labour. Speaking in Brisbane earlier this morning, Taylor said the tariff “shouldn’t be happening”: I tell you what should be happening, the prime minister should be sitting down with the president of the United States and saying this is not good enough. He needs to be clear to the president of the United States this is an unacceptable thing to do with one their very greatest friends and allies. You can’t do this to us. The Australian trade minister, Don Farrell, immediately called for the US to change course last week when the tariffs were announced, saying they were unjustified: Israeli siblings who fear breaking law in Gaza under IDF owed protection by Australia, tribunal finds Three Israeli citizens facing conscription into the Israel Defense Forces have been granted the right to reapply for protection visas in Australia, after a government tribunal found they held a genuine fear they would be forced to break international humanitarian law in Gaza. The Administrative Review Tribunal found the punishment the young adults could face from the state of Israel – including imprisonment as conscientious objectors – would amount to persecution. Part of a family group, three siblings faced mandatory national service if they were returned to Israel, and held a genuine belief they would be forced to “engage in breaches of international humanitarian law”. The tribunal found there were “credible allegations that Israel’s military operations in the Gaza Strip are in breach of international humanitarian law” and that international opinion was that the IDF’s actions in Gaza were disproportionate. It found the three siblings were refugees facing persecution from the state of Israel, and Australia had a legal obligation to protect them. Read more: The Victorian premier, Jacinta Allan, has indicated she will fight any attempt to oust her as Labor leader despite the party’s factions agreeing overnight that she lacks the support of the majority of her caucus. Under Labor’s rules, if Allan does not step down as leader and is challenged, a weeks-long process will occur in which both parliamentary Labor caucus and rank-and-file members vote. Votes are split evenly: 50% of the weight goes to MPs and 50% to party members. In a letter to the Victorian Labor state secretary, Steve Staikos, obtained by Guardian Australia, Allan said she intended to be a candidate if such a ballot occurred. The letter reads: I refer to media speculation regarding the leadership of the Victorian Parliamentary Labor Party and am writing to request that you ensure that the Victorian Labor Party is prepared to conduct an election for the leadership of the State Parliamentary Labor Party in the event an election is required. As you are aware the Victorian Labor Party rules require State Secretary to provide administrative support to ensure the effective conduct of a ballot of all eligible party members. chineseTitle: 澳大利亚新闻直播：具有里程碑意义的廉政公署开始对新南威尔士州自由党腐败指控进行调查
chineseContent: 新南威尔士州前总理的兄弟试图利用他们的影响力来帮助悉尼开发商，ICAC 听说回到新南威尔士州 ICAC 的 Rosny 行动，助理律师 Peggy Dwyer SC 博士更详细地描述了正在调查的指控。在描述该监管机构的调查时间表时，她透露，警方在 WhatsApp 上转交了前总理多米尼克·佩罗泰 (Dominic Perrottet) 的两个兄弟让-克洛德 (Jean-Claude) 和查尔斯·佩罗泰 (Charles Perrottet) 的通讯，两天前，总理本人向廉政公署提交了腐败指控。这位前总理是在凯利维尔自由党议员雷·威廉姆斯 (Ray Williams) 2022 年在议会发表演讲后采取这一举措的，他声称逃亡的房地产开发商让·纳西夫 (Jean Nassif) 与高级自由党人士会面，据称他们获得了大量资金，以安排新议员当选为 Hills Shire 议会。德怀尔在听证会上表示，在威廉姆斯发表演讲的前一天，警方将合法截获的“多米尼克·佩罗特的两个兄弟”的通讯交给廉政公署。这些合法截获的信息还表明，纳西夫先生与多米尼克·佩罗泰特的两个兄弟有联系，而且他正在寻求利用他们与多米尼克·佩罗泰特的关系，协助将建筑专员大卫·钱德勒免职。多米尼克·佩罗特没有被指控有任何不当行为。让-克洛德、查尔斯·佩罗特和纳西夫此前否认有任何不当行为。廉政公署 (Icac) 今天开始就新南威尔士州自由党的腐败指控举行“罗斯尼行动”听证会。作为“罗斯尼行动”的一部分，廉政公署正在调查三项指控，首先是自由党高级人士“索取或接受”捐款，包括来自禁止的捐款
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于全球新闻信号，适合用于观察外部环境、政策变化、地缘风险和市场情绪。
